title: Dictate to Grimm and a roomier mobile chat
summary: Grimm's chat box now has a microphone button (and ⌘D / Ctrl+D shortcut) for live AssemblyAI dictation when ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY is set, with Cancel, Edit, and Send controls. On phones, Grimm packs the top nav and session bar into single slim rows, tucks + New, Workers, and host resources behind the ⋯ button, hides the desktop keyboard hint, and collapses the top nav and chat tabs while the virtual keyboard is open so the conversation owns the screen.
mediaAlt: A mobile local demo of the Grimm chat page showing the compact single-row site nav and session bar with the details toggle, the full chat thread visible, and the composer actively dictating with Listening status and Cancel, Edit, and Send buttons.

title: Model variants of a workflow
summary: Make model variant, in a workflow's editor, makes a copy that changes only the orchestrator model and its own trigger (such as its own email address). It keeps the original's steps and prompt: each later change to the original reaches the variant too. The variant's editor says which workflow it follows, with Detach to make it a plain copy again.
mediaAlt: A workflow editor in a local demo, headed Email Task (GPT-6.2 Sol Ultrafast), with the note that it is a model variant of Email Task: its steps and prompt come from there, only its orchestrator model and trigger are its own, and a Detach button.

title: Grimm UX polish and inline live-worker cap editor
summary: Grimm now includes an inline worker-cap stepper popover in the header (replacing the browser prompt) that validates inline, updates all open tabs live, and notifies the running manager when the cap changes. The composer moves image and file drafts inside the box with a paperclip button, live upload progress, send locking and per-session draft persistence; the thread adds boxed tool icons, centered update pills, callout notices, pulsing status dots, kind-colored bus borders, a tablet Quota drawer and 390px phone refinements.
mediaAlt: A local demo of the Grimm page showing the polished thread, an image draft inside the composer with live status, opening the inline Workers cap stepper popover, and saving a new cap with a live header update and green confirmation toast.

title: Approve and monitor workflow runs from Grimm
summary: The Grimm manager can now propose starting a saved workflow (intelligence grimm ctl workflow request) without launching it on its own. Each request appears as a live card in the Grimm thread where you can edit the task input, approve and start the run, or reject it from your signed-in browser. Once started, the card streams live status, step progress, gate outcomes, waiting questions or sign-off prompts, and a link to the run page, while waking Grimm on run milestones.
mediaAlt: A local demo of the Grimm thread showing two live workflow cards: an approved Ship Feature run waiting on owner sign-off with passed step and gate badges and a Review & sign off button, and a pending Nightly Audit request with Approve & start, Edit input, and Reject buttons.

title: Live host resources in the Grimm header
summary: The Grimm page header now shows a live resource pill in the upper right for the session's host: CPU, memory, disk, and load or pressure with color thresholds. Hover on desktop (or tap on a phone) for a detail card with CPU average and peak, 1/5/15-minute load per CPU, memory and swap headroom, Paseo cgroup memory, disk I/O and busy time, PSI pressure, filesystems, OOM kills, the session's busiest agents, and the reading's age (stale readings are marked). Updates stream live via the session's SSE feed.
mediaAlt: A local demo of the Grimm page showing the live host resource pill for dev-box in the upper right of the header with its hover detail card open, displaying CPU, load, memory and swap, Paseo cgroup memory, disk I/O, PSI pressure, filesystems, OOM kills, and busiest session agents.

title: Grimm starts in desk
summary: A new Grimm session now starts in desk by default: the Start a Grimm session form on the home page fills in the picked host's desk checkout, so you can just start and chat. Grimm works in its own worktree of desk on a grimm/ branch, never in desk's main checkout. Type another path to use a different repository.
mediaAlt: The Start a Grimm session form in a local demo, with host-1 picked and the repository field already filled in with that host's desk checkout.

title: Grimm is the home page
summary: Grimm now opens when you open Intelligence: start a session on a repository on any connected host and talk to Grimm, an Opus 5.5 manager that hires named workers on your plans, watches them and reports back. Its words, the team, plans, bus and each worker's live log stream as they happen, on a phone too. Messages mid-turn, Stop, images and a per-session worker cap (20 by default) are in the chat. The old home page is now Hosts.
mediaAlt: A local demo of the Grimm page: a message asks for a CSV to Markdown tool, Grimm streams its plan, hires athena on Codex and hermes on Claude Opus 5.5, the team panel and message bus fill in, and an update arrives when the workers finish.

title: Password fields when a run needs a secret
summary: When a workflow run needs a password or API key from you, its ask now shows a password field for each one on the run page (a text area for a multi-line key). Intelligence keeps the value encrypted, fetchable only by agents on the run's host, wipes it when the run ends or after 7 days, and never puts it in the run's events or transcripts. The run page's Secrets card shows when each was fetched and lets you delete one early.
mediaAlt: A waiting workflow run's ask in a local demo: Requested secrets, marked Temporary, with masked fields for a Stripe API key and webhook signing secret, a masked multi-line Deploy key, Show buttons and Store secrets & reply.

title: Readable titles for API-triggered workflow runs
summary: Runs started through the workflow API now show readable titles on the Workflows page instead of a YAML frontmatter schema line. Intelligence strips leading YAML frontmatter automatically, extracts concise titles for structured Contract Check and Contract Fix runs, and lets API callers pass an explicit one-line title field on POST /api/workflow-api/runs.
mediaAlt: The Workflows page in a local demo showing API-triggered Contract Check and Contract Fix runs with readable titles instead of a YAML frontmatter schema line.

title: Deterministic key-to-repository routing for workflows
summary: A workflow can now choose its repository from a table of routes that you review, instead of asking an agent. In the workflow editor, open Find the project and choose Mapped from input keys. Each route sends a list of keys, such as contract IDs, to one repository on the host. You can also name an outline file in Git. Intelligence then checks the tree that the caller sends against the latest outline in Git, so a key can use its parent's route. A run with an unmapped key, keys for two repositories, or a tree that does not match Git does not start.
mediaAlt: The Intelligence workflow editor in a local demo showing Find the project set to Mapped from input keys (deterministic) with reviewed repository routes and Git tree verification configured for demo-contracts.

title: Require explicit browser approval on workflow sign-off steps
summary: Sign-off steps can now enable Require explicit browser sign-off approval in the workflow editor. Waiting runs show an Approve sign-off button beside Send reply (Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends a plain reply without approving). Only clicking Approve sign-off from your signed-in browser records a signoff_approved event that unlocks advancing past the step; plain replies, rejections, email replies, API-key calls, skips and earlier approvals before a re-ask or send-back are refused.
mediaAlt: A waiting Release sign-off run in a local demo showing the Owner sign-off ask card with the primary Approve sign-off button beside Send reply and the note explaining that plain replies or rejections do not authorize landing.

title: Trigger, stream and control workflows with scoped API keys
summary: Any workflow can now enable Allow triggering via API beside its existing trigger so external repositories and services can start runs idempotently, list and inspect runs, read agent transcripts, stream live events and transcripts over resumable SSE, and reply, send input, cancel or retry runs. Open a workflow's Trigger panel, check Allow triggering via API, save, and issue or revoke scoped keys there.
mediaAlt: The workflow editor's Trigger panel for Agreement review in a local demo showing Allow triggering via API checked beside the manual trigger and the scoped API keys list with active and revoked keys.

title: Pick the host a new task runs on
summary: The New task box on the Workflows page now has a Host menu beside Workflow. Leave it on Workflow's host to run where the workflow says, as before, or pick any of your online hosts to run this one task there. Offline hosts show but cannot be picked. A workflow that always works in one repository needs that repository on the host you pick. Retrying a failed run keeps the host it ran on.
mediaAlt: The New task box on the Workflows page in a local demo: a task typed, the Workflow menu on its workflow's host example-host-1, and the new Host menu set to example-host-2 beside Submit task.

title: Workflows shows what needs you and what is running first
summary: The Workflows page now leads with your runs, not the workflow definitions. Under the task box, Needs you shows each run waiting on your reply with its question, the step it is at and how long it has waited. In progress lists every live run with its step (Step 2 of 7), a progress bar and what it is doing now, plus how many runs are at each step. The full runs history follows, and the workflows are at the bottom.
mediaAlt: The Workflows page in a local demo: two Needs you cards with their questions, then In progress with per-step counts and live runs showing their step and progress bar.

title: Install Intelligence as a standalone app with native push notifications
summary: Intelligence is now an installable Progressive Web App with a home-screen icon, standalone window and Web Push notifications. On Android Chrome, tap the menu and choose Add to Home screen / Install app, then open Account → App & notifications to enable notifications on that device. You get native notifications when a workflow asks for your reply, a run fails, or a busy host goes silent, and tapping one opens the relevant page.
mediaAlt: The Account page's App & notifications section in a local demo showing the notification controls and a subscribed Android Chrome device.

title: Runs wait on model quota instead of asking you
summary: When a model group has no eligible model, blocked workflow runs now show waiting on model quota and resume automatically with a fresh suggestion once quota returns, instead of asking you one by one or stalling. Runs already parked on a model-availability ask also resume on their own with the ask resolved. If a host stays blocked for 30 minutes, Intelligence sends at most one host-level phone notification listing the waiting runs.
mediaAlt: A workflow run page showing Running status, Current activity waiting on model quota, and What happened recording no eligible model for the group.

title: Retry failed runs and auto-rerun after workflow fixes
summary: Failed workflow runs now have a one-click Retry button on the run page that starts a new run on the workflow's latest version with the same input. When an email or voice memo run fails, Intelligence pushes a phone notification right away with the error in plain words, and saving a new version of its workflow automatically re-runs recent failed-to-start runs.
mediaAlt: A failed voice memo run in a local demo showing the Retry button in the page header and the start error banner below.

title: Attach images and files to workflow replies
summary: The reply and Additional input boxes on a workflow run page now support attaching images and arbitrary files by clicking + Attach, dragging and dropping, or pasting from the clipboard. Attached files appear as removable previews and are saved under .factory-scratch/attachments/ for the orchestrator to open. The shared file picker also accepts arbitrary files across task, agent and chat forms.
mediaAlt: A workflow run reply box attaching a screenshot and a PDF file, showing removable preview chips before sending them to the orchestrator.

title: Workflows switch a host to a Claude login with quota
summary: When a host's active Claude login cannot serve a model group, and another login cswap holds on that host is the best choice, the next suggestion asks the host to switch every Claude agent on it to that login. The worker gets that login once the host reports the switch. Plans → Model groups shows such a group as After a login switch, and the login as Needs login switch. Hosts switch at most once every 15 minutes.
mediaAlt: Plans → Model groups in a local instance: Claude Opus 5.5 shows After a login switch, with one login marked Needs login switch and the active login at its quota reserve.

title: Run a workflow's Codex agents at Fast or Ultrafast speed
summary: In a workflow's editor, a Codex orchestrator or project finder now has a Speed setting: Normal, Fast or Ultrafast. The agent starts at that speed and keeps it for every turn. Faster speeds use more of the plan. Other providers have no speed setting.
mediaAlt: The workflow editor's Orchestrator panel with provider codex, model gpt-6.2-sol, thinking high and Speed set to Ultrafast.

title: Per-host plan auth status across multiple hosts
summary: Each plan card on Hosts and Plans now shows every host signed into that login with its own slot and auth status (active, standby, expiring, broken, read error or stale), plus host-attributed errors. Hosts without cswap fall back to claude auth status so they join active-login tracking, model-group suggestions and expiry alerts with host-appropriate re-auth commands.
mediaAlt: A local Intelligence instance showing the Hosts page with per-host plan auth badges across box-alpha and box-beta (active, expiring, broken) and the login alert banner.

title: Antigravity is back with Gemini 4 Neon Medium
summary: Antigravity is available for new launches again. In Plans → Model groups, Gemini 4 Neon Medium replaces Extra High where it was already a member of Frontier Models. A suggestion requires a host that reports the model, an active login and fresh quota.
mediaAlt: Plans shows Gemini 4 Neon Medium suggested in Frontier Models, with Antigravity quota meters below.

title: Send a follow-up to a running workflow
summary: Use Additional input on a running or stalled workflow run to send a note to its orchestrator. Sending a note resumes a stalled run at its current step. The note and its delivery status appear under What happened. If the orchestrator is asking you a question, use the reply box.
mediaAlt: A running workflow receives a follow-up asking for keyboard shortcuts, and the run history shows delivery to the orchestrator.

title: Gemini 4 Neon Extra High in Frontier Models
summary: Plans → Model groups lists Gemini 4 Neon Extra High in existing Frontier Models groups with a reported Antigravity Gemini quota pool. Suggestions require an enabled provider, the model in the host's signed-in Antigravity catalog, and fresh quota. Other Neon and Hydrogen variants appear in model pickers as eligible hosts report them.
mediaAlt: The Frontier Models group in local Plans, with Gemini 4 Neon Extra High listed and marked Provider disabled

title: Alerts when a busy host goes silent
summary: When a host with queued, running or waiting workflow runs stops reporting for 10 minutes, a red note under the top bar on every page names the host, how long it has been silent, how many runs wait on it and its last recorded OOM kills. Intelligence also sends one phone notification through PDW, and one more when the host reports again. Idle hosts never alert.
mediaAlt: A local demo: the red note under the top bar saying a throwaway host stopped reporting, with its silent time, waiting runs and OOM kills

title: Agents recover when a login expires
summary: When a Claude or Codex login stops working, a note under the top bar on every page names the login and host, counts the agent turns it stopped, and shows how to sign in again without touching the live login, with Copy command and Mark fixed. Once a working login is active, Intelligence resumes each stopped agent with the same model, or asks its orchestrator to. Logins ending within 5 days are flagged too. Plans lists the agents a login stopped.
mediaAlt: A local demo: the broken-login note with its fix steps and the safe sign-in command, the Plans page's list of stopped agents, and Mark fixed clearing the note

title: Email follow-ups keep their context
summary: A reply email within 24 hours continues the earlier run's agent, keeping its research and numbers. Replies say "Correction:" and explain why when they change an earlier answer. On the run page, What happened links each follow-up to the earlier run.
mediaAlt: A local demo run's What happened section showing a follow-up resuming the earlier run's orchestrator, with links to that run

title: Filter workflow runs by status
summary: On Workflows, use the tabs above Runs to see Running, Queued, Needs you, Stalled, Completed, Failed or Canceled runs. Each tab counts the full history. Status filters work with search and pagination and stay in the URL so you can bookmark or share them.
mediaAlt: The Runs list switching between Running, Queued and Completed with counts on every status tab

title: Reopen a rejected proposal
summary: Rejected a proposal by mistake? Open it in Proposals and choose Reopen to return the same snapshot to review. You can also ask its answer agent to reopen or repropose it in the discussion. Reopening checks for workflow changes and expiry; approval is still required.
mediaAlt: A rejected proposal in a local demo showing the Reopen button next to Ask a question

title: Run estimates from workflow history
summary: The runs table and run page fill missing ETAs from recent workflow step times, marked as estimates. Sign-off shows waiting on Zach; external waits name the person or party. Activity updates record their own time and hide old typed time annotations.
mediaAlt: Run page with an activity update and a history-based completion time marked as an estimate

title: See what each run is doing now
summary: The runs table and run page now show the latest activity, when it was reported and an ETA. Updates older than 30 minutes are marked stale. Orchestrators report progress with the workflow status command, including during long waits.
mediaAlt: Phone-sized run page showing release checks in progress, the age of the activity update and an estimated completion time

title: Runs on one deliverable steer instead of racing
summary: An email or voice memo run now checks the runs already going before it builds. When one is working on the same deck, link or thread, it hands its request to that run instead of rebuilding in parallel. A run's page shows what it claimed and which runs steered into it; a steered run says which run answers it.
mediaAlt: A run page's first step: Claimed a deck link, then another run steered into this run because it is about the same deck, with its request

title: Runs that hand off or need no answer stop showing as unanswered
summary: A run that hands its request to another run (a voice memo folded into a running deck run) now counts as answered when that run answers, and Workflows shows which run answered it. A run whose input was not a request records why, and Workflows shows the reason instead of flagging it. Runs from before answer tracking no longer count as unanswered.
mediaAlt: Workflows runs table: one run answered via another run, one steered run still awaiting that run's answer, and one marked No answer needed: A recorded meeting, not a request

title: Plans shows the last four weekly peaks
summary: Each login on the Plans tab now lists its four latest weekly peaks. Older weeks are folded under Show older weeks, one click away, so the page is about a third shorter.
mediaAlt: A login's weekly peaks on Plans: four rows, then Show 10 older weeks, which opens to list the rest

title: Branches, diff sizes and sub-agents on Hosts
summary: On Hosts, each workspace now shows its Git branch and the size of its uncommitted changes (lines added and removed), and each agent's sub-agents sit directly under it, marked with ↳. The agent page's Agents sidebar lists them the same way.
mediaAlt: A host on Hosts: a workspace with its branch feat/rate-limit and +84 −19, and a running sub-agent indented under its parent agent

title: See what holds a host's run queue
summary: When runs are queued for room on a host, the Workflows page now names the next one and why it waits, for example that runs waiting for your sign-off hold the memory it needs. Each run's memory estimate now comes from its own workflow's past runs, so a quick email answer is no longer sized like a Factory Task in the same repository.
mediaAlt: The Workflows page with a banner: 3 runs queued on host-1, the next run and its reason, ending with waiting for 2 sign-offs to free memory

title: Times in your own time zone
summary: Every time Intelligence shows, on run timelines, schedules, plans, host monitoring, proposals, email and account pages, now reads in your browser's own time zone and format. Hover a time to see the full date, time and zone. Relative times such as 5m ago are unchanged.
mediaAlt: A workflow run page whose step and What happened timelines show times such as Nov 11, 6:34 PM in the browser's time zone

title: See when workflow requests get answered
summary: Workflows and each run show minutes to the first checked answer, with unchecked sends listed separately. Email and voice requests without checked answers are flagged when they finish; overdue requests are also readable in SQL. Task runs can record answers without owing a reply. Agents use the workflow answer command.
mediaAlt: A completed example email workflow with its step marked done, an unchecked send at 6 minutes and a checked answer at 15 minutes, plus the sent message identifiers

title: Start a queued retry now
summary: When a run's start retry is waiting in its host's queue for capacity, its run page has a Start retry now button. It sends the retry at once, ahead of the queue, and What happened records it. It still counts as one of the three retries, and if it fails it is handled like any other failed retry.
mediaAlt: A run page showing Retry 1 of 3 queued with a Start retry now button; after the click it shows Retry 1 of 3 sent and the timeline says the retry was started by hand, ahead of the queue

title: Let urgent workflows skip the queue
summary: Choose Priority in the workflow editor’s Trigger panel: Automatic follows the trigger, Immediate skips capacity checks, and Normal waits. Automatic email requests and voice memos start immediately, even after changing a task workflow’s trigger. Use Start now on a queued run for a one-time bypass.
mediaAlt: Workflow editor Trigger panel showing Automatic priority after changing a task workflow to a voice memo trigger

title: Page through and search workflow runs
summary: Workflows now lists every run, 50 a page, with Newer and Older links under the table, so older runs are no longer cut off. The search box beside Runs finds runs across all history by any words in their summary, prompt, workflow, status, host, project or branch.
mediaAlt: The Runs list on Workflows: a search for a word narrows it to the matching runs, then Clear and Older page back through history

title: Disk I/O, free space and load in Host monitoring
summary: Host monitoring now charts each host's load against its CPU count, how busy its disks are and how fast they read and write, and lists every local filesystem with its used, free and total space. Hosts on the home page show their load and free disk, and a disk busy more than half the time.
mediaAlt: Host monitoring for a demo host: load, disk busy and disk throughput charts, and a filesystems table with used, free and total space

title: Recover stalled workflow runs
summary: Workflows now nudges an idle orchestrator with its current step when no worker or reply is pending. After two unsuccessful continuations, the run shows Stalled with a reason. Open Workflows or the run page and choose Resume to continue on the same orchestrator and step. Admission queues, startup retries and permission prompts keep their existing rules.
mediaAlt: A sample workflow run marked Stalled, with its recovery reason and Resume button on the run page

title: Queue runs by repository memory needs
summary: The host queue estimates RAM from successful runs of the selected repository, with headroom and a default for repositories without history. The run page shows the estimate. Active runs keep unused memory reserved, and startup retries use the same estimate and FIFO queue.
mediaAlt: A queued application build showing its 10 GiB repository memory estimate and the host memory capacity reason

title: Choose worker models with reusable groups
summary: Create model groups on Plans or Workflows, then insert their tokens into step instructions. Each suggestion balances reachable plan logins using current quota usage, with a model and thinking level you choose. Tokens stay stable when groups are renamed; shared edits affect future suggestions.
mediaAlt: Model groups on Plans, with Frontier and Google frontier tokens, current suggestions, plan labels, and Copy and Edit controls

title: Review proposed workflow runs before they start
summary: MCP clients and host agents can now propose workflow runs. Open Proposals to review the full task and saved workflow, then approve or reject. Nothing starts before approval. Approved proposals link to the resulting run; changed workflows require a fresh proposal.
mediaAlt: A pending workflow run proposal showing its summary, Approve run and Reject controls, full quoted task input and saved workflow

title: Start workflows from voice memos
summary: Choose a PDW voice memo trigger in the workflow editor. Matching recordings start runs with a 1000-character transcript preview and a command to fetch the full transcript. Workflows → Voice memos shows polling status, decisions and links to the matched workflow and run.
mediaAlt: Voice memo history with polling status and a recording linked to its workflow and run

title: Review workflow changes and ask questions
summary: Open Proposals to review a Markdown summary, highlighted changes, and approval controls. Ask a question and an agent answers in the same thread, using desk for context when available. Replies appear automatically, with status and retry controls if an answer cannot start or does not arrive.
mediaAlt: A workflow proposal with its summary and highlighted added instruction, followed by a question and an agent's answer in the discussion thread

title: What's New
summary: A What's New tab now lists each feature as it ships, newest first, with a short summary and a demo. When there are some you have not seen, the tab shows how many and a note appears under the top bar; opening the tab or dismissing the note marks them seen.
mediaAlt: The What's New tab showing 7 unseen features; opening it shows them, newest first, and the count goes away

title: Read Intelligence from MCP clients
summary: Intelligence is now a read-only MCP server at /mcp. Make a token under Account → MCP connections, add it to an MCP client, and that client can query your hosts, agents and workflow runs with SQL. It can read but never change anything.
mediaAlt: Account → MCP connections: Create MCP token shows the MCP URL and a new token (blurred here) once, and lists it as active

title: Attach images to tasks and messages
summary: Add screenshots and other images to a workflow task, a new agent or workspace, or a message in an agent's chat: pick, paste or drop them. The agent gets each image as a file in its worktree.
mediaAlt: Typing a task on Workflows, then attaching two screenshots, which appear as removable thumbnails under the prompt

title: See how long each workflow step took
summary: A workflow run's page now shows how long it spent on each step, and how many times it came back to one, with the current step counting up.
mediaAlt: A workflow run's steps: done steps show their time and how many times the run was on them, and the running step counts up

title: Unattended agents get past permission prompts
summary: When an unattended workflow agent stops on a permission prompt, Intelligence now answers it with an audited denial so the agent carries on, and shows any prompt it could not clear.
mediaAlt: An agent page marked “permission recovery stuck” next to its running and needs-attention badges

title: Start workflows from email
summary: Connect a Gmail mailbox under Workflows → Email, and an email that matches a workflow's senders and filters starts a run of it. Replies in the thread go to that run.
mediaAlt: Workflows → Email: the connected mailbox and what came in, one email ignored as bulk mail and one that started a run; its link opens the run with the email thread

title: Dictate instead of typing
summary: Press ⌘D (or Ctrl+D, or the mic button) in the chat box, a task box or a new agent prompt to speak instead of type. Press it again in an empty box to send.
mediaAlt: Clicking the mic in the task box: the words appear as they are said, then Edit stops and leaves them in the box
